How do light and sound travel to our eyes and ears?
light source. Something that makes its own light. The Sun, a lamp, and a candle flame are light sources.
reflect. To bounce back. A mirror reflects light. A far wall can reflect sound.
shadow. A dark shape made when an object blocks light.
opaque. Blocks all light. Light cannot pass through. Wood and cardboard are opaque.
vibrate. To move back and forth very fast. A guitar string vibrates when you pluck it.
pitch. How high or low a sound is. A tiny bell has a high pitch. A big drum has a low pitch.
echo. A sound that bounces off a wall and comes back to you.
Light comes from a light source , like the Sun or a lamp. Light travels in straight lines . It hits things and bounces off. Some of that light goes into our eyes. That is how we see !

Is the Moon a light source? It looks bright at night. But the Moon makes no light of its own. Sunlight hits the Moon and bounces off. Then it reaches my eyes. So the Moon is not a light source. It reflects light.

Why can't you read a book in a totally dark closet? The book is there. Your eyes work. But no light hits the book. So no light bounces from the book into your eyes. Now turn on a flashlight. Light bounces off the page and into your eyes. Now you can read!

Some things block light. They are opaque , like wood or your body. A dark shadow forms behind them. Clear things, like window glass, let light pass through. A smooth, shiny mirror reflects light. Reflect means to bounce back.

Why does my shadow change during the day? In the morning, the Sun is low in the sky. My body blocks the light at a slant, so my shadow is long. At noon, the Sun is high. My shadow is short. My shadow is always on the side away from the light.

Where will the shadow be? A lamp is on the left side of a toy dinosaur. Light travels in straight lines from the left. The dinosaur is opaque, so it blocks the light. The shadow falls on the right side, away from the lamp.

Sound is made when something vibrates . Vibrate means to move back and forth very fast. The vibrations travel through the air to your ears. Inside your ear, your eardrum vibrates too. Then you hear! Fast vibrations make a high pitch . Slow vibrations make a low pitch.
I put my fingers on my throat and hum. I feel a buzz. That buzz is my throat vibrating. Now I stop humming. The buzz stops, and the sound stops too. So sound and vibration go together.

You shout "Hello!" in a big, empty gym. A moment later, you hear "Hello!" again. Why? The sound traveled to the far wall. It bounced back to your ears. A sound that bounces back is an echo . Sound can reflect, just like light!

Same toy. Same wall. Same flashlight. The toy stayed 12 inches from the wall. Only the distance from the flashlight to the toy changed. At 24 inches away, the shadow was 6 inches tall. At 12 inches, the shadow was 8 inches. At 6 inches, the shadow was 12 inches. At 3 inches, the shadow was 20 inches tall.

Lewis Latimer. An inventor and expert drafter. His parents had escaped slavery. He taught himself to make careful drawings of machines. He drew the patent drawings for Alexander Graham Bell's telephone . Later he found a better way to make the thin carbon filament inside light bulbs. His bulbs lasted longer. He helped bring electric light to cities like New York and London.

Dr. Patricia Bath. An eye doctor and inventor from Harlem in New York City. Many people go blind from cataracts . A cataract is when the lens of the eye turns cloudy. She invented the Laserphaco Probe . It uses a laser, a strong beam of light, to remove cataracts. In 1988, she became the first Black woman doctor to get a patent for a medical invention.

James West. An engineer who studied sound. As a boy, he liked to take radios apart. At Bell Labs, he and Gerhard Sessler invented a small, low-cost microphone in 1962. A microphone turns sound vibrations into electric signals. Their kind of microphone has been used in billions of phones, computers, and hearing aids.

Ibn al-Haytham. A scientist who lived in Basra, in what is now Iraq, and in Cairo, Egypt. Long ago, many people thought eyes sent out beams to see. He tested that idea. He showed that light travels in straight lines into our eyes. He did experiments in a dark room with a tiny hole. He wrote the Book of Optics .
